input.content: STAGE 1 — goal: orient in the repo before proposing. read: working dir listing. observed: see below. reasoning: need existing SID/quantizer/hyperbolic code to avoid duplicating a mechanism. open: find RQ-VAE / Stage2/Stage3 code.

STAGE 2 — goal: fix three distinct coupling sites. read: no file access permitted (read/glob denied, empty workdir); relied on the scope contract text. observed: contract lists assignment/Sinkhorn, hierarchy, residual/transition as suggested positions, implying other agents will take those; also mentions 'inherited unused hyperbolic code' as a non-qualifier. reasoning: choose three sites not on the suggested list — (A) the straight-through backward path, (B) the atom-position/shape parameterisation (behaviour-derived radial shells), (C) the reconstruction target (gyro-barycentre). open: write full specs with derived constants and frozen-scale costs.

STAGE 3 — IDEA A result (GEO-STE-GATE). Coupling: gradient returned by the STE is w_b(i)*(lambda_p/lambda_u)*gyr[u,-p](g_u); behaviour = standardised out-transition entropy from training split; geometry = conformal factor + gyration of the Poincare ball. Removal of either changes the update, hence the SID assignment. Cost: O(B d) per step, <1% Stage2. Distinct because geometry sits in the backward pass, not in a loss or an assignment cost.

STAGE 4 — IDEA B result (GEO-SHELL-RQ). Coupling: atom radius r_lg = (N-B_g)/(N+B_g) from measured hierarchical branching of the training transition graph, fed into m = exp_0((2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) r) u_hat), atoms e = exp_m(eps). Radius is derived (Sarkar embedding of a tree with B_g leaves), no tuned constant. Cost: one-off precompute plus O(K L d) projection per step.

STAGE 5 — IDEA C result (GYRO-TARGET-RQ). Coupling: reconstruction target b_i = exp_{p_i}(eta_i * mean_j log_{p_i}(sg(p_j))), eta_i = c_i/(1+c_i) from measured top-1 successor probability, successors = immediate next items in training sessions only. Changing either term changes what the encoder is asked to encode, hence the SID. Cost: O(E d) refresh once per epoch, ~0 marginal per step. Risk: identity smoothing, bounded by eta<=1/2.

const ans = `IDEA: GEO-STE-GATE
TITLE: Curved straight-through gradient: Poincare parallel transport of the quantizer gradient, gated by measured transition branching.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE copies the codebook gradient back to the encoder as an identity map, i.e. as if the latent were flat. Items near the ball boundary and items in dense transition regions are then updated with the wrong magnitude and the wrong direction, so coarse prefixes stop being behaviourally coherent.
NOVELTY: The curvature acts in the BACKWARD pass (the STE), not in a loss, not in an assignment cost and not in the codebook. The behaviour signal multiplies the same transported vector, so the two are one expression.
CHANGE: Replace the identity STE by the parallel transport of the reconstruction gradient from the item's ball point to the reconstruction point, rescaled by the ball conformal factors, multiplied by a per-item behaviour gate.
SPECIFICATION: forward = tangent-space RQ with Poincare assignment: v0=z_e; for l=1..L: p_l=exp_0(v_{l-1}); k_l=argmin_k d_c(p_l,e_{l,k}); a_l=log_0(e_{l,k_l}); v_l=v_{l-1}-a_l; zhat=sum a_l; phat=exp_0(zhat); u=exp_0(z_e); L=||log_phat(u)||^2+commitment. backward: dL/dz_e := w_b(i)*(lambda_phat/lambda_u)*gyr[u,-phat](g_u), g_u=dL/du.
COST: O(B d) for one gyration (two Mobius additions) plus two conformal scalars; B=1024, d=64 -> ~0.1 MFLOP per step on top of an encoder step of order 1e2-1e3 MFLOP. <0.5% of Stage-2 step time, ~1-3 min over 72000 steps; one extra scalar (curvature) parameter; Stage 3 unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: If radial depth really controls how much an item may move, the transported gradient changes the per-item update norm by a factor spread of >1.5x and the coarse-prefix transition coherence rises, which shows up as Stage-3 recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: Transport may be a near-scalar rescale in low dimension (gyration trivial for d<=3), reducing the idea to a learning-rate multiplier; the gate sign (high branching -> larger step) could be wrong; lambda blow-up near the boundary.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transition branching entropy H_out(i) of each item, from the training split only.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: For consecutive pairs (i,j) in training sessions, C_ij counts; p_ij=C_ij/sum_j C_ij; H_out(i)=-sum_j p_ij log p_ij; items with no outgoing edge get H=mu_H. mu_H, sigma_H measured over all training items.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: H_out is a frozen offline table computed from training sequences only; validation and test interactions never enter it, and the table is built before Stage 2 starts and never refreshed.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball B_c^d, c=softplus(rho) initialised at 1; distance d_c; exp/log maps; parallel transport PT_{x->y}(g)=(lambda_x/lambda_y)gyr[y,-x]g with gyr[u,v]w=(-(u+v))+(u+(v+w)).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the straight-through estimator that connects the quantizer to the encoder during Stage-2 training.
COUPLING PATH: behaviour gate -> multiplied into the transported gradient -> encoder parameter update -> encoder output z_e -> assignment p_l -> SID codes. Removing the gate makes every item move identically; removing the transport makes the ball flat.
COUPLING EQUATION: dL/dz_e(i) = [1+tanh((H_out(i)-mu_H)/sigma_H)] * (lambda^c_phat / lambda^c_u) * gyr[u,-phat](g_u)
OBSERVABLES: per-item update-norm ratio vs radial depth (should correlate), mean c||p||^2 during training, per-level code usage entropy, prefix transition coherence, Stage-3 test recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: w_b == 1 for every item, transport unchanged.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c forced to the Euclidean branch, PT replaced by identity, plain STE, gate unchanged.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full expression above.
SPEC EQUATIONS: as in SPECIFICATION; gate computed once offline, detached (constant per item, no gradient through H_out).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: input z_e (B x d), phat, u, per-item gate w_b; output transported tangent gradient (B x d) written into the encoder's autograd path.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp ||z_e|| <= (1-1e-3)/sqrt(c) before exp_0; artanh argument clipped to 1-1e-7; if ||u|| or ||phat|| < 1e-6 use PT=I; c clipped to [1e-3,10]; gate in (0,2) by construction; NaN guard falls back to identity STE for that step.
END IDEA

IDEA: GEO-SHELL-RQ
TITLE: Codebook atoms placed on radial shells whose radius is the measured branching of the training transition tree.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE spreads every level's codebook over the same latent volume, so a coarse prefix that covers a huge behavioural subtree occupies no more room than a leaf that covers three items. The generator then has to memorise which of 256 equally sized prefixes is broad.
NOVELTY: The behaviour statistic sets the RADIUS of each atom inside the curved ball (atom positions), not the assignment weight and not a loss; the radius is a closed-form tree-embedding quantity, so no constant is tuned.
CHANGE: Each atom is an anchor plus a small learnable tangent offset; the anchor is the Frechet mean direction of its training-interaction community placed at hyperbolic radius r_lg, and every step the atoms are geodesically projected back into their shell.
SPECIFICATION: symmetrise training transition counts A=C+C^T, build an L-level community tree (recursive Leiden/normalised cut) with N leaves; for level-l community g, B_g = measured number of leaf descendants; r_lg=(N-B_g)/(N+B_g); rho_lg=(2/sqrt(c))artanh(sqrt(c) r_lg); u_hat = unit direction of the Frechet mean of the frozen item content embeddings in g; m=exp_0(rho_lg u_hat); e=exp_m(eps); forward RQ identical to baseline but distances d_c; after each optimiser step project e along the geodesic diameter to the shell [rho_lg-delta, rho_lg+delta].
COST: one-off tree + Frechet precompute over 24556 items (minutes, CPU); per step only the O(K L d)=256*3*64 ~ 5e4 elementwise projection plus the d_c terms already present. <1% of Stage-2 wall clock; no extra Stage-3 cost.
HYPOTHESIS: If the ball radius allocated to a prefix should match how many leaves it must separate, then broad behaviour communities will occupy large-radius shells and their token will become predictable from a short history; prefix-conditional accuracy rises and Stage-3 recall@10 clears 0.065.
RISKS: The community tree may disagree with the content geometry and put anchor directions in the wrong cones; hard shell projection can freeze atoms; the Sarkar radius saturates near 1 for huge subtrees and loses resolution.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Hierarchical branching (leaf mass B_g) of the training directed-transition graph.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Training sessions only: consecutive pairs -> C; A=C+C^T; L-level Leiden partition; B_g = number of level-L leaves weighted by their item mass under g; N = total leaf mass.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The tree is built once from the training split before Stage 2 and is frozen; no validation/test sequence contributes an edge, and item content features used for the anchor direction are the frozen encoder inputs, not interaction-derived quantities from val/test.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball with curvature -c (fixed at c=1 unless the shared scalar is enabled), geodesic diameters, exp/log maps, Frechet mean via Karcher iteration.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the codebook parameterisation and in a per-step geodesic projection of the atoms (quantization time).
COUPLING PATH: measured B_g -> r_lg -> hyperbolic radius rho_lg -> anchor position -> d_c assignment -> code index -> SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: e_{l,k}=exp_{m_{l,k}}(eps_{l,k}), m_{l,k}=exp_0((2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) (N-B_g)/(N+B_g)) u_hat_{l,k})
OBSERVABLES: radial distribution of atoms per level, code usage vs B_g, prefix predictability, Stage-3 test recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: every community gets B_g = N/K, i.e. uniform shells r_lg = (K-1)/(K+1) per level; geometry and offsets unchanged.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Euclidean branch: anchors at radius (B_g/N)^(1/d), arithmetic Frechet mean, Euclidean distance, linear projection to the shell.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full coupled expression.
SPEC EQUATIONS: as above; delta = half the gap between adjacent anchors' rho.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: input training transition counts and frozen item content embeddings; output L codebooks of K atoms in B_c^d and, per forward pass, code indices per item.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp r_lg to [1e-3,1-1e-3]; keep ||eps|| <= 0.25*(rho_lg-rho_parent); artanh clip; empty communities fall back to the parent anchor; Karcher iteration capped at 10 with step norm clip.
END IDEA

IDEA: GYRO-TARGET-RQ
TITLE: The autoencoder reconstructs a geodesic-shifted successor barycentre instead of the item itself.
MOTIVATION: Many items are interchangeable given the same successor distribution; giving each its own code wastes generator capacity on distinctions the behaviour does not make. Behavioural role, not item identity, is what the next-item predictor needs.
NOVELTY: The behaviour signal changes the RECONSTRUCTION TARGET inside the curved ball; it is not an extra loss term, not a reweighted assignment and not a codebook prior.
CHANGE: The reconstruction target of item i is a point on the geodesic from its own ball point toward the hyperbolic mean of its training successors, displaced by a fraction fixed by the item's measured transition concentration.
SPECIFICATION: S_i = immediate next items of i in training sessions; c_i = max_j p(i->j); eta_i=c_i/(1+c_i) in [0,1/2]; b_i=exp_{p_i}(eta_i * (1/|S_i|) sum_j log_{p_i}(sg(p_j))); loss=d_c(phat_i,b_i)^2+commitment; successor points p_j taken from a stop-gradient table refreshed every epoch.
COST: successor table O(E d) refresh once per epoch (E ~ 1e5 edges, d=64 -> 6e6 flops, amortised ~2.5e5 per step) plus one extra exp/log per item O(B d). Negligible against Stage 2; a few MB of CSR storage; Stage 3 unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: If SIDs encode behavioural role, items with the same successor set collide onto one code and the generator's prefix prediction becomes easier; measured by the number of distinct codes per successor-set cluster and by Stage-3 recall@10 > 0.065.
RISKS: Over-smoothing can merge genuinely distinct items and collapse recall; the momentum table can lag and create a moving target; eta depends on p(i->j) which is noisy for rare items.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Sequential co-consumption, specifically the set of immediate successors of each item and the concentration of that successor distribution.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From training sessions only: for each adjacent pair (i,j) add j to S_i; c_i = max_j count(i,j)/|S_i|.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: S_i and c_i are computed from training sequences only and frozen; the successor point table is refreshed from training items' forward passes only; no val/test sequence or label is ever read.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball curvature -c, exp/log maps at the item point p_i, geodesic interpolation, d_c reconstruction loss.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the reconstruction target of Stage-2 training, hence in the gradient that shapes the encoder and the codebooks.
COUPLING PATH: behaviour concentration eta_i -> length of the geodesic displacement from p_i -> target b_i -> reconstruction loss -> encoder and codebook update -> SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: b_i = exp_{p_i}( eta_i * (1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} log_{p_i}(sg(p_j)) ), eta_i = c_i/(1+c_i)
OBSERVABLES: mean number of items per code, code reuse across items with identical successor sets, prefix conditional accuracy, Stage-3 test recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: eta_i = 0 so b_i = p_i, the standard autoencoder target.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Euclidean branch: b_i = p_i + eta_i * mean_j (p_j - p_i), Euclidean reconstruction loss.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full coupled expression.
SPEC EQUATIONS: as above, plus the commitment term of the baseline RQ-VAE.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: input item i, its successor set S_i and concentration c_i, current point p_i and successor table; output target b_i and the reconstruction gradient.
SAFEGUARDS: eta <= 1/2 by construction; clamp eta to 0 when |S_i|<2; detach the successor table; clamp ||b_i|| <= (1-1e-3)/sqrt(c); log-map argument clipped; skip the batch if the target norm is non-finite.
END IDEA`;
await tools.progress.append_progress({content: "STAGE 6 — FINAL ANSWER (complete).\n" + ans});
return "saved final";

BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: For consecutive pairs (i,j) in training sessions, C_ij counts; p_ij=C_ij/sum_j C_ij; H_out(i)=-sum_j p_ij log p_ij; items with no outgoing edge get H=mu_H. mu_H, sigma_H measured over all training items.

HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the codebook parameterisation and in a per-step geodesic projection of the atoms (quantization time).

IDEA: GYRO-TARGET-RQ
TITLE: The autoencoder reconstructs a geodesic-shifted successor barycentre instead of the item itself.
MOTIVATION: Many items are interchangeable given the same successor distribution; giving each its own code wastes generator capacity on distinctions the behaviour does not make. Behavioural role, not item identity, is what the next-item predictor needs.
NOVELTY: The behaviour signal changes the RECONSTRUCTION TARGET inside the curved ball; it is not an extra loss term, not a reweighted assignment and not a codebook prior.
CHANGE: The reconstruction target of item i is a point on the geodesic from its own ball point toward the hyperbolic mean of its training successors, displaced by a fraction fixed by the item's measured transition concentration.

HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the reconstruction target of Stage-2 training, hence in the gradient that shapes the encoder and the codebooks.

ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Euclidean branch: b_i = p_i + eta_i * mean_j (p_j - p_i), Euclidean reconstruction loss.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full coupled expression.

SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: input item i, its successor set S_i and concentration c_i, current point p_i and successor table; output target b_i and the reconstruction gradient.
